chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

For the adulterer there are six characteristics: three in the world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in the world, it removes the light of the face, causes poverty, and hastens destruction; and as for those in the Hereafter, it is the anger of the Lord, the evil reckoning, and eternity in the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the six consequences of adultery in this Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes the penalties of zina into immediate worldly signs and ultimate Hereafter consequences, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the holistic impact of sin on both physical appearance and spiritual destiny. The 'loss of facial radiance' (dhahab bi-nur al-wajh) is a well-known concept in Islamic tradition indicating a visible dimming of one's spiritual light, while 'hastened death' (u'jil al-fana') suggests a premature end to one's lifespan as a divine decree. This dual-layered punishment underscores the belief that major sins affect the believer's state in this world before manifesting fully in the next.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For the adulterer there are six characteristics, three in the world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in the world, so it removes the light of the face, and inherits the poverty, and hastens the destruction; and as for those in the Hereafter, so it Angers the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and the evil Reckoning, and the eternity in the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy fm ‘Abd Allah ibn Maymun al- Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his father who has said that

one who commits fornication faces six troubling issues, of which three are in this world and three in the next life. In this world it takes away light and beauty from his face, brings poverty and quicker death. In the next life, it is the anger of Allah, worse account and living in the fire forever.’”
